name: Quarter Squat
description: The quarter squat limits knee flexion to approximately 25-30 degrees of travel, keeping the torso more upright and the load on the quadriceps near full extension. It is used for sport-specific power training (since most jumping and sprinting occurs in this partial range), for post-surgical rehabilitation where full depth is contraindicated, and for accommodating resistance training with bands or chains where supramaximal loads are used in the strongest portion of the lift.

execution.starting_position: Set up as for a barbell back squat, with the bar on the upper back and feet shoulder-width apart.
execution.setup_instructions: May use safety pins set high in the rack to limit depth, or use a box just above parallel as a guide.
steps: Step 1: Unrack the bar and stand with feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out.
Step 2: Begin the descent by pushing the hips back and bending the knees.
Step 3: Descend only until the knees reach approximately 25-30 degrees of flexion (about a quarter of full depth).
Step 4: Drive upward through the full foot, extending the knees and hips to return to standing.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale and brace before descent, exhale on ascent.
common_mistakes: Excessive forward lean of the torso
safety_considerations: The partial range concentrates high loads on the knees — ensure proper alignment
Useful clinically but should not replace full squats for general training
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Intentionally limited to ~25-30 degrees of knee flexion.
